title: Redis memory management
context: How does Redis manage memory, and what happens when it is full?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Redis keeps data in RAM, so `maxmemory` caps how much it may use. Keys with a TTL are removed when they expire: some passively on access and some by periodic sampling. When memory reaches the cap, the eviction policy decides: noeviction returns errors on writes, allkeys-lru and allkeys-lfu evict any key, volatile-* policies evict only keys with a TTL. Choose the policy for the use: a cache wants allkeys-lru, while a store of must-keep data wants noeviction with alerts.

points.title: maxmemory and policies
points.why: Without a cap, Redis grows until the host runs out of memory.

points.title: Expiry is not instant
points.why: Expired keys are removed lazily and by sampling, so memory use lags the TTL.
